If you ran the example script successfully, you've got most of this in "restable" and "teststable".  E.g. the example script:


#######################################################
# Your results should be:
#######################################################

# > restable
# 
#                 LnL numparams            d            e         j
# DEC           -34.5         2 3.504546e-02 2.835632e-02 0.0000000
# DEC+J         -20.9         3 1.000000e-12 1.000000e-12 0.1142811
# DIVALIKE      -33.1         2 4.474416e-02 1.000000e-12 0.0000000
# DIVALIKE+J    -21.1         3 2.001000e-09 1.000000e-12 0.1157199
# BAYAREALIKE   -40.3         2 1.738085e-02 3.040188e-01 0.0000000
# BAYAREALIKE+J -21.6         3 1.000000e-12 1.000000e-12 0.1081158

#######################################################
# The p-value of the LRT (Likelihood Ratio Test) tells you whether or not you can reject the
# null hypothesis that DEC and DEC+J confer equal likelihoods on the data
#
# AIC and AICc model weights are also shown, giving a sense of the relative probability of the two models.
#
# (One could easily do model weights between all 6 models, but this is not done here; s
#  see Brian O'Meara's AIC webpage: http://www.brianomeara.info/tutorials/aic )
#######################################################

# > teststable
# 
#              alt        null LnLalt LnLnull DFalt DFnull DF Dstatistic    pval        test       tail  AIC1  AIC2 AICwt1  AICwt2 AICweight_ratio_model1 AICweight_ratio_model2
# 1          DEC+J         DEC -20.95  -34.54     3      2  1      27.19 1.8e-07 chi-squared one-tailed  47.9 73.08   1.00 3.4e-06                 294893                3.4e-06
# 11    DIVALIKE+J    DIVALIKE -21.09  -33.15     3      2  1      24.13 9.0e-07 chi-squared one-tailed 48.17  70.3   1.00 1.6e-05                  63797                1.6e-05
# 12 BAYAREALIKE+J BAYAREALIKE -21.09  -33.15     3      2  1      24.13 9.0e-07 chi-squared one-tailed 48.17  70.3   1.00 1.6e-05                  63797                1.6e-05
#


You should be able to figure out how to calculate model weights and interpret them from:

======================================
Advice On Statistical Model Comparison In Biogeobears
http://phylo.wikidot.com/advice-on-statistical-model-comparison-in-biogeobears

Model Selection Using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC)
http://www.brianomeara.info/tutorials/aic
====================================== 

...one can do the calculations in Excel easily.



Alternatively, teststable already has the AIC values and pairwise model weights. If you wanted a six-way comparison instead of pairwise, you could do this, starting from restable:

===============

# Look at the results table
restable

# Calculate the AIC values
AICvals = getAIC(LnL=restable$LnL, numparams=restable$numparams)
AICvals

deltaAICs = get_deltaAIC(AICvals=AICvals)
deltaAICs

rel_likes_AIC = rel_likes_from_deltaAICs(deltaAICs=deltaAICs)
rel_likes_AIC

Akaike_weights = get_Akaike_weights_from_rel_likes(rel_likes_AIC=rel_likes_AIC)
Akaike_weights

# Final table of Akaike weights (relative probability of the models, keeping in 
# mind THESE ARE ONLY RELATIVE TO THE INCLUDED MODELS, THERE COULD BE BETTER
# MODELS YOU DIDN'T THINK TO INCLUDE)

restable2 = cbind(restable, Akaike_weights)
restable2

# The weights add up to 1, as they should
sum(restable2$Akaike_weights)


# Percentages
percentage_wt = round(restable2$Akaike_weights * 100, digits=2)
restable3 = cbind(restable2, percentage_wt)
restable3

===============


Cheers!
Nick



 
2014-09-03 5:34 GMT+02:00 Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>:

Hi! This means you need to change this part of the example script:


==============
# Divide the tree up by timeperiods/strata (uncomment this for stratified analysis)
#BioGeoBEARS_run_object = section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table=TRUE, plot_pieces=FALSE)
# The stratified tree is described in this table:
#BioGeoBEARS_run_object$master_table
==============


To this:

===============
# Divide the tree up by timeperiods/strata (uncomment this for stratified analysis)
BioGeoBEARS_run_object = section_the_tree(inputs=BioGeoBEARS_run_object, make_master_table=TRUE, plot_pieces=FALSE)
# The stratified tree is described in this table:
#BioGeoBEARS_run_object$master_table
===============

...so that your tree is actually sectioned for the stratified analysis...

Can I post this to the listserv to help others (sans your files)? Cheers!

Cheers!
Nick
